name: Hamlyn driver
full_name: Hamlyn hands-on robotic catheter driver for learning from demonstration (pre-CathBot)
group: Imperial College London, Hamlyn Centre (G.-Z. Yang; H. Rafii-Tari, W. Chi, C. J. Payne, J. Liu, C. Riga, C. Bicknell)
versions: 2012 IROS force-feedback system for catheterisation (Payne, title only); 2013 MICCAI GMM/GMR learning with the driver; 2014 MICCAI hierarchical-HMM cooperative catheterisation; 2018 IJCARS non-rigid-registration trajectory transfer; from 2020 the Hamlyn LfD work runs on CathBot (chi2020_collaborative uses 'the CathBot system')
target_anatomy: aortic arch cannulation (innominate, left common carotid) in silicone phantoms
devices_driven: one standard catheter (operator handles the guidewire manually in the 2013 shared-control scheme)
translation_detail: friction-roller (pair of friction wheels coupled to one servomotor)
rotation_detail: second servomotor rotates the frame that holds the catheter; two Dynamixel MX-28 servomotors, PID (rafiitari2013 Sec. 2.3; chi2018 Sec. Experiments)
force_sensing: none on the driver; ATI Mini40 6-DOF sensor under the phantom for evaluation (chi2018)
haptics_leader: hands-on master: proximal position-sensing unit that reads natural catheter motions (two DOF); no force feedback in these papers
imaging_compat: NDI Aurora 6-DOF EM sensor at the tip; 2-D projected image for the operator
validation_detail: 2013: 12 robotic cannulations per learned model (expert and intermediate) across 4 inexperienced operators; 2018: cross-validation over three type-I aortic-arch phantoms under dry, continuous and pulsatile flow, forces vs four experts
key_numbers: 2018 success 98.1% dry and 94.4% continuous flow; mean contact force -33.3% and force SD -70.6% vs manual (chi2018 abstract)
sim2real_detail: none found (policies learned from real phantom demonstrations)
